title: Large clusters for small models — Daniel Svonava, Superlinked
talk_summary: Svonava argues small open-source models now match frontier quality on narrow tasks and that serving a fleet of them requires a pull-based centralized queue rather than a top-down router, plus per-task model selection and tuning.

takeaways.technique: Pull-based work queue instead of push routing
takeaways.what_they_do: A gateway annotates requests and drops them into a shared queue (NATS JetStream); workers pull and form their own batches based on their own load prediction, rather than a central router pre-deciding placement.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of the top down router trying to uh you know fill in the local cues just right, which is basically impossible... the workers uh rather pick up the task of forming their own batches
takeaways.numbers: centralizing the queue doubled cluster throughput; top-down routers got GPU utilization only 20-30%

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of one general model, slice the workload into tasks and pick the best-fitting open model per task, validated with evals and light adaptation; a single agent used nine different models.
takeaways.evidence_quote: figure out slice of tasks from the generalized model workload and then per task you figure out which model in the open source fits the task the best

takeaways.technique: Auto-research tuning loop with bundled configs
takeaways.what_they_do: They run automated research loops that measure and tune model/runtime performance, and ship a full tuned config per model so users never do parameter sweeps.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have auto research loops for uh adding support for new models and for their performance... when we ship support for a model it has all the tuning done
takeaways.numbers: a LoRA that took 80 cents to train improved retrieval quality 18% on German legal texts

takeaways.technique: Self-host embeddings/task models for high-volume work
takeaways.what_they_do: Run small open models on a single GPU for embeddings, NER, synthetic-data generation instead of managed endpoints, getting huge throughput at low latency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you could be like having one GPU and push half a million tokens per second into that thing... as opposed to like pushing all of that into a managed embeddings endpoint
takeaways.numbers: hundreds of thousands of tokens/sec embeddings on one RTX Pro 6000; low tens of ms vs hundreds of ms for hosted APIs

takeaways.technique: Pack multiple small models per GPU with lazy load/eviction
takeaways.what_they_do: Abandon one-worker-pool-per-model; pin some models but lazily load and evict others based on memory pressure so many small models share GPUs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: pack models on the same GPU is faster... you want to also do u basically uh lazy loading and eviction uh as a kind of function of memory pressure
